chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Uzafir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he was asked about the earnings of the female lamenter, and he said: 'It is permissible for her [to earn it] by striking one of her hands upon the other.'
ai.seo_question: Is the income of a female professional mourner permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that the earnings of a professional lamenter are permissible provided she performs the specific gesture of striking one hand upon the other, which distinguishes her act as legitimate mourning rather than mere performance. This hadith highlights the Shia juristic approach to contextualizing pre-Islamic cultural practices, validating them when aligned with the intent of mourning the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the principle that the permissibility of earnings depends on the nature of the act and its social recognition as a valid service.
